newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Sidor ready for privatization-official.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Sidor ready for privatization-official.

text.p: Venezuelan steel company Sidor is ready for privatization, which will go ahead as soon as Congress approves the company's sale contract, the head of the government's privatization program said Wednesday.
"We've finally managed to prepare Sidor technically for sale," Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) President Alberto Poletto told reporters in Congress after presenting the Sidor sale terms.
"The only thing we need to go ahead with the sale is Congressional approval of the contract terms," Poletto said.
The auction of Sidor could take place with 45 days of Congressional approval, he said.

Under the contract a controlling 70 percent stake will be sold to a consortium at auction. The remaining 30 percent will be held for later sale to workers, local companies and possibly the public through a share issue.

Poletto said the sale of Sidor would be beneficial to Venezuela since the contract included a commitment to maintain steel supply to the local market and invest at least $300 million in upgrading the plants and another $80 million in removing toxic wastes.
Eleven companies have already qualified to bid for Sidor from Mexico, Brazil, Japan, South Korea, Argentina and Venezuela.
The sale of Sidor is expected to face a tough passage through Congress, where many legislators have said they will oppose it.
